results.corrected_title: NBER study by David Autor and Google researchers: AI drafting help left lasting skill gains for senior patent lawyers only
results.corrected_summary: NBER Working Paper 35720, by David Autor (MIT) and six Google co-authors, reports a pre-registered three-month randomized trial with 133 patent lawyers at 11 US IP firms. A custom AI drafting tool raised drafting quality by 0.38 SD at 90 days, and the gains were larger for juniors while they used it. On a later redlining test without AI, previously treated senior lawyers (7+ years) beat controls by 0.45 SD. Junior lawyers showed no average gain. The paper has not been peer reviewed.
key_facts: NBER WP 35720, issued September 2026 and revised October 2026
133 lawyers at 11 US IP firms that draft patents for Google
AI access raised drafting scores by 0.38 SD at 90 days
Without AI, senior lawyers who had used AI scored 0.45 SD above controls; juniors showed no average gain
91 of the 133 completed the test without AI; not peer reviewed
results.issues: STALE: NBER lists the issue date as September 2026, before the 2026-10-09 window. Fortune's 10 October article is later coverage, and the October revision is not a substantive new development. The exact September day is unknown, so event_date uses the 1st of the month as a placeholder.

results.corrected_title: Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark at IMF/World Bank meetings: internal model says AI could lift US GDP almost 50% by 2030
results.corrected_summary: Speaking at the IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok on Saturday 17 October, Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark said one of Anthropic's internal models suggests that, under certain assumptions, US output could rise almost 50% by 2030, to about $44 trillion from just over $30 trillion today. He admitted the figure 'sounds very outlandish'. He also said AI is already costing jobs in highly exposed areas such as call centres and customer service, and that the window to put safeguards in place has shrunk to 'a small number of years'.
key_facts: Venue: IMF/World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, Saturday 17 October 2026; reported by Reuters
An internal Anthropic model projects US GDP of about $44tn by 2030, up from just over $30tn, if AI keeps improving and new industries emerge
Clark: the figure 'sounds very outlandish, I know'
AI is already causing job losses in call centres and customer service, but adding jobs in scientific research
He warned the window for safeguards is 'a small number of years' and called for strict oversight of AI use in biology
results.issues: The US News URL timed out when opened. The facts were confirmed through the BusinessDay copy of the same Reuters report. The GDP number is an internal, assumption-heavy scenario, not a forecast.

results.corrected_title: Bloomberg: Russia, Iran and China use generative AI to amplify disinformation ahead of US midterms
results.corrected_summary: Bloomberg News reported on 14 October 2026, citing people familiar with US intelligence and independent researchers, that Russia, Iran and China are using generative AI tools to boost disinformation ahead of the 3 November midterms. Bloomberg reviewed 130 fabricated videos and doctored newspaper front pages from the Russian 'Matryoshka' network, published between 10 September and 9 October, that targeted Democratic candidates. Some imitated ABC and CBS broadcasts or used fake celebrity likenesses, and bot networks inflated their view counts. Iran-linked networks pushed anti-Republican content, while Chinese operations such as Spamouflage used AI to run thousands of fake accounts.
key_facts: Bloomberg article by Natalia Drozdiak, published 14 October 2026
Bloomberg reviewed 130 fake videos and front pages from 10 September to 9 October, mostly flagged by Antibot4Navalny
The fakes mimicked ABC and CBS news segments and used synthetic likenesses of celebrities such as De Niro and Cher; Democrats were targeted in 20 of 35 Senate races
ChatGPT and Claude were named as tools adversaries used to plan propaganda campaigns
China's embassy said it opposes political disinformation; the Russian and Iranian sides did not comment
results.issues: The full Bloomberg article is paywalled. Core claims confirmed by the Bloomberg Government excerpt, Bloomberg's own video and the Kyiv Post. Network, ABC/CBS and celebrity details rest on the Kyiv Post account. Candidate details dropped: 'CNN-style clips' and 'Storm-1679' (vendor-only), OpenAI's 8 October bans (different operations, before window) and the Cathy Kipp complaint (unrelated domestic case).
